name: Chip supply
value: TSMC halts some China orders at 16nm and below
summary: US rules from 19 Nov led TSMC to halt some Chinese orders at 16nm and below; Samsung reported to pause some shipments
state: US Commerce Department rules effective 19 Nov removed a compliance route that let some Chinese chip designers use advanced foundry services without licences, and TSMC has halted orders at 16nm and below unless customers obtain US licences (TrendForce, 20 Nov). TSMC and Samsung are reported to have paused some consumer-chip shipments to Chinese customers (TrendForce; Yahoo Finance). New controls keep Watch; TSMC and Samsung output itself is not disrupted.
for_you: Chinese phone and electronics makers that rely on TSMC or Samsung for mid-range chips may face delays, which can affect launch timing for some devices. Supply to other markets is not reported to be affected.
rubric_hit: New US export controls = Watch; no disruption to TSMC/Samsung output

sources.title: TrendForce — TSMC, Samsung reportedly pause China consumer chip shipments under new US rules
Yahoo Finance — TSMC is halting some China chip orders as a new US rule kicks in

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
